issues.detail: The Greek 'κατεργασαμενοι' (kateergasamenoi) is a perfect passive participle describing the state of having 'worked out' or 'accomplished' something. The Vietnamese 'làm xong mọi sự' (finished everything) is too broad; in this context, it refers specifically to the 'working out' of one's faith/character (the spiritual work mentioned in the preceding verses), not just completing general tasks.

The Greek 'δυνηθητε' (dynēthēte) is a middle/passive form of 'to be able' (be empowered/enabled). The Vietnamese 'có thể' captures the ability, but the specific nuance of being 'empowered' or 'enabled' by the source is slightly softened.
